# JI Java public API baseline 0.1.0

Status: Stage 2 `0.x` incubation baseline. Breaking changes are permitted only when documented here; no compatibility shim is required before 1.0.

## Public artifacts

- `ji-ai-api`: `ModelRef`, immutable `Message`/`Content`, `Usage`, `ModelRequest`, `ModelResponse`, `ModelStreamEvent`, `ModelProvider`, JI cancellation token/source, `ToolSchema`, Provider Profile/model catalog, credential reference/resolver/material, and structured sensitive/redaction types.
- `ji-agent-api`: `AgentRuntimeBuilder`, `AgentRuntime`, `AgentSession`, `AgentRun`, `AgentEvent`, `SessionOptions`, synchronous `ToolDefinition`, `RuntimeConfiguration`.
- `ji-session-api`: revision-CAS `SessionRepository`, immutable `SessionSnapshot`, and Stage 2's versioned Pi-compatible `SessionDocument`/`SessionCodec` contracts plus shared Repository TCK. The document mutation log owns Entry, LaneRecord, Lane and fact sequence; adapter projections do not become a second fact source.
- `ji-security-api`: non-serializable secret/master-key values, external key source and credential/OAuth ports.
- `ji-extension-api`: capability-based `WorkspaceProvider`, versioned/cancellable `PermissionDecider`, `ToolExecutionPolicy`, ordered `ToolInterceptor`, fail-closed `ToolRetryContract`, stable resource/source/revision/scope identities, `PromptContributor`, `ContextSource`, `SkillSource`, strict prompt renderer/assembler, data-only `Skill`, and hash-bound `ProjectTrustStore` contracts.
- `ji-artifact-api`: SHA-256 identity, full scope/reference DTO、direct/resumable commands、Range/ETag result、quota/retention limits、validation report 和 `ArtifactStore` port；known failure 由 `ArtifactErrors` 生成版本化 `JiException/JiError`。
- `ji-telemetry-api`: explicit callback-owned `TelemetryContext`/`TelemetrySpan`、span/event/metric vocabulary、allow-list policy、NOOP 和 deterministic recording TCK reference；实现不得泄漏 backend 类型。
- `ji-error-catalog`: generated `ErrorCode` and `JiError`.

## Lifecycle and threading

- The application owns `AgentRuntime`; closing it closes Sessions, Provider, Store and an internally-created executor. A caller-supplied executor is not closed.
- `AgentSession` is thread-safe for state observation. It accepts one active Run; a concurrent prompt fails synchronously instead of being silently queued.
- `prompt` returns immediately with an `AgentRun`. `completion()` settles after the durable terminal transition. `abort()` is cooperative and idempotent.
- Provider and Tool effects execute off the Session commit boundary on bounded-by-caller/runtime executors. Repository writes remain short revision-CAS critical sections.
- Tool batches complete ordered preflight before starting effects; any sequential Tool serializes its batch, otherwise effects may run concurrently with limits of 8 per Session and 32 per Host. Waiting work uses a bounded queue. Policy, permission, workspace and operation revision are rechecked immediately before the effect; stale completion cannot commit.
- Prompt contributors run before a Provider attempt on the effect executor, in deterministic `priority/source/id` order. Each contributor and the assembled prompt have explicit token budgets; one contributor failure is isolated and source provenance remains attached to accepted fragments.
- Local resource scanning is bounded, progressive, cancellable, and single-flight per catalog. Project context, skills, templates, settings and extension metadata remain unavailable until an exact project/resource-set fingerprint is trusted; each load rechecks canonical path/content hash against the discovery generation, and one TOCTOU change invalidates the whole protected projection. Ready snapshots own immutable bytes; the next coalesced refresh detects set membership changes without a duplicate full scan.
- `Flow.Publisher` callbacks run on a Session-owned event executor so slow listeners cannot occupy Provider/Tool effect threads. Each subscriber buffer is bounded at 256 events; producers apply `SubmissionPublisher` backpressure instead of dropping lifecycle events or growing an unbounded queue. Listener failures are isolated by `SubmissionPublisher`.
- All public DTO collections are copied. `transcript()` and repository snapshots are immutable projections, never an alternate fact source.
- Telemetry callbacks are admitted synchronously exactly once; span settlement follows sync/async callback settlement, and adapter/exporter failure is suppressed without changing returned values or failure identity. Telemetry locator/native context is diagnostic-only and must not be persisted as Session state.
- Artifact writes publish content identity and scoped reference only after atomic completion; resumable upload/retry and reference/pin metadata are durable across adapter restart. `ArtifactStore` is thread-safe at its atomic metadata/object boundary; large I/O remains outside Session actor ownership.

## Error contract

- Public synchronous and asynchronous known failures use public `JiException`, whose `error()` returns generated `ErrorCode`, structured parameters, and allowed optional `traceId`, `retryAfter`, and `currentRevision` fields. Provider and Tool raw response bodies, headers, credentials and stack traces are not part of the public error.
- Calling `AgentRuntime.newSession` or `loadSession` after close throws `runtime.closed` with required `resource=agent-runtime`; calling `OpenAiProvider.stream` after close throws `provider.closed` with required `provider=openai`. Both are synchronous public `JiException` failures and do not expose implementation exceptions.
- Known mappings include runtime/provider closed, Provider authentication/permission/rate/timeout/unavailable/request/redirect/invalid-response/context failures, Tool missing/execution/policy/queue, workspace boundary/stale/revision/path, edit match conflict, shell environment/execution, operation cancellation/stale completion, Session not found/active Run, Permission denied/expired/revision conflict, command payload conflict, resource path/hash/trust/limit/invalid states, prompt contribution/template/budget failures, Artifact invalid/quota/hash/not-found/corrupt/unavailable/workspace-source rejection, and protocol invalid/slow-consumer.
- CLI JSON diagnostics remain on stderr and use documented exit classes; Stage 1 implements input/internal behavior, with complete mapping continuing in later stages.

## Baseline procedure

The local publication gate produces JAR, POM, sources and javadoc in `build/stage1-repository`. `scripts/verify-stage1-consumer.ps1` creates a repository-external Gradle project which depends only on those artifacts and completes a deterministic two-turn Tool loop. `scripts/generate-api-baseline.mjs` uses the built JARs plus JDK `jar`/`javap` to generate [`0.1.0-signatures.json`](0.1.0-signatures.json), including top-level and nested public classes, constructors, methods, return types and parameters while excluding compiler-generated anonymous/builder implementation classes; `scripts/verify-api-baseline.mjs` regenerates it in a temporary directory and compares bytes. The Markdown contract and machine-readable signatures form the initial 0.x diff baseline; a binary compatibility promise starts at internal 1.0.
